title: Is it okay to run shirtless in public?
description:
Do you run without a a shirt on ever? Lots of people have opinions on this topic and in some parts of the world it’s something you’re just not allowed to do.

We hear from runners around the world for their take on the decision to run without a shirt one - for both men and women.

And Yijin Shim from BBC Korean tells us about how in South Korea “no shirtless running” signs have been popping up after more runners have been going shirtless in a heatwave.

summaryEn: In this episode of What in the World, presenter Hannah Gelbart examines the debate over running shirtless in public. Runners from the UK, India, and the US discuss how running without a shirt or in a sports bra provides comfort, prevents chafing, and aids in heat relief, while also addressing body confidence and gender disparities in public expectations. Yejin Shim from BBC Korean explains that rising heatwaves in South Korea have led to increased shirtless running, resulting in "no shirtless running" signs at parks like Yeouido Hangang River Park and Namsan Park due to local etiquette preferences. Additionally, the episode highlights local laws in places such as Venice and Sorrento in Italy, where walking or running shirtless away from the beach can incur fines, reminding runners to respect regional rules.
